members.name: tx-paras
members.para: If the connection is not open, it is opened first and closed (not disposed) when the transaction completes, even if it fails. A connection that was broken is closed and opened again, so it is closed afterwards too. A connection that was already open is left open. A failure while closing is ignored, as by then the transaction has already been committed or rolled back. To keep a connection open across several operations, open it before calling.

An exception thrown by the action, or a cancellation, rolls the transaction back and propagates. A transaction that is not committed is rolled back by disposing it, which is the standard ADO.NET pattern; the .NET documentation for notes that this is provider specific. The transaction is always disposed before the connection is closed, as some providers (for example Microsoft.Data.Sqlite and MySqlConnector) only roll back an uncommitted transaction on dispose while the connection is still open. The action should not commit or roll back the transaction itself; completion is handled here. When no isolation level is given, is used.

members.name: tx-async-para
members.para: The transaction is begun with BeginTransaction, not BeginTransactionAsync, which returns a plain : this keeps the type flowing to the action. It is then disposed with DisposeAsync, committed with CommitAsync, and the connection closed with CloseAsync, except on .NET Framework (net472), which does all three synchronously. The token is checked just before the commit, and the commit itself is not canceled once it has begun: cancelling part-way through would leave the outcome unknown.
